chunks: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
'Establishment of a hadd (prescribed punishment) is better than the rain of forty mornings.'

key_terms.إِقَامَةُ حَدٍّ: establishment/execution of hadd — the implementation of the Quranically prescribed punishments for specific major crimes such as theft, unlawful sexual intercourse, and false accusation
key_terms.حَدّ: hadd (pl. hudud) — the fixed punishments prescribed by the Quran and Sunnah for certain crimes
key_terms.مَطَر: rain — used here as a metaphor for widespread worldly benefit and blessing

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about establishing hudud punishments compared to rainfall?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (saww) declares that the execution of a divinely ordained hadd punishment is more beneficial to society than forty days of rainfall. This hadith underscores the Islamic legal philosophy that proper enforcement of God's prescribed laws purifies society from moral corruption and upholds justice, just as rain purifies and nourishes the earth. In the early Muslim community, this teaching affirmed that consistent application of divine law — rather than leniency in major crimes — is the foundation of a righteous social order.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said; ‘
Establishment of the Limit (Hadd) is better than the rain of forty mornings’.
